/skills/agent/claude-code.title: Claude Code Skills: Where They Live & How to Install
/skills/agent/claude-code.description: Claude Code reads Agent Skills from .claude/skills or ~/.claude/skills. Install one in 30 seconds, see six skills people use, and fix one that never triggers.
/skills/agent/claude-code.body:
Claude Code doesn't need another prompt library. It needs files it can read at the moment a task starts. That's what an Agent Skill is: a folder with a SKILL.md (name, description, instructions) plus any templates or scripts the workflow needs. Claude Code scans the folders below at session start and pulls a skill in when your request matches its description.

Where Claude Code looks for skills

ScopePathUse it for
Project.claude/skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.mdSkills that ship with a repo and should be shared with the team
User~/.claude/skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.mdSkills you want in every project

Project-level wins when both exist. The folder name is the skill's identity, so keep it lowercase and hyphenated.

Install a skill in 30 seconds

  1. Copy the skill folder into .claude/skills/ (or ~/.claude/skills/).
  2. Confirm the file is at .claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md — not one level deeper.
  3. Restart Claude Code, then ask: "What skills do you have?"
  4. Trigger it with a task, not the skill name: "Make an OG image for this article."

The most common install mistake is unzipping into a folder that contains another folder, so Claude Code sees .claude/skills/<name>/<name>/SKILL.md and never loads it.

Six skills Claude Code users actually install

SkillWhat it producesInstalls
Device-Canvas Product LaunchA launch film built around your product UI489
Hand-Drawn Visual NotesSketched notes and explainer frames383
Cadence Marketing LandingA complete marketing landing page299
GrokBot AvatarA stylised avatar set286
Field Notes DeckAn editable presentation deck257
Notion Style OG Image1200×630 social previews197

When a skill doesn't trigger

  • Check the description, not the name. Claude Code matches on the description. If it says "helps with design", it won't fire on "make an OG image".
  • Check depth. SKILL.md must sit exactly one level under the skills folder.
  • Check scope. A project skill only exists inside that project.
  • Check for a stale session. Skills are discovered at start; restart after adding one.

FAQ

Do skills cost extra tokens? Only the name and description are loaded up front; the body is read when the skill is activated. Long skills are cheaper than they look.

Can I edit a skill I bought? Yes. It's a text file. Keep your edits in a fork so updates don't overwrite them.

Skills or MCP? Skills teach a workflow; MCP connects a tool. Most production setups use both — see Skills vs MCP.

Where do I start? If you build pages, start with build a landing page. If you publish content, start with create an OG image.

/skills/agent/codex.title: Codex Skills: Folder Setup and 6 Skills Worth Installing
/skills/agent/codex.description: Codex loads skills from ~/.codex/skills or .codex/skills in a repo. Here is the exact folder layout, a 30-second install, and six skills that survive real work.
/skills/agent/codex.body:
Codex works best when a repeated job is written down once. A skill is that written-down job: a SKILL.md with a name, a description that tells the agent when to use it, and the steps or assets to follow. Because Codex runs in your terminal and your repo, skills become part of the project rather than a chat you have to re-explain.

Where Codex looks for skills

ScopePathUse it for
User~/.codex/skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.mdYour personal toolkit, available in every repo
Project<repo>/.codex/skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.mdSkills a team shares through version control

If the same name exists in both, keep one — duplicated names make behaviour unpredictable.

Install in 30 seconds

  1. Drop the skill folder into ~/.codex/skills/.
  2. Verify the path ends in /SKILL.md.
  3. Start a new Codex session.
  4. Ask for the outcome ("build a pricing page for this product"), not the skill name.

Skills that hold up in real repos

SkillWhat it producesInstalls
Slate Admin ConsoleA working admin dashboard UI287
Chalkboard InfographicA hand-drawn explainer graphic267
Yellow Sketchnote DeckA sketchnote-style deck239
Editable Visual DeckSlides you can still edit after export182
Beacon SaaS LandingA SaaS marketing page191
Activity Calendar ChartAn interactive activity heatmap186

What makes a Codex skill different from a prompt

A prompt is consumed once. A skill is discovered, reused, and versioned. That matters most for work you do weekly: release notes, changelogs, screenshot sets, landing page variants. Put the stable part in SKILL.md and the variable part in the request.

Troubleshooting

  • Skill ignored: the description is too abstract. Rewrite it around the verbs a user would type.
  • Skill partially applied: the body references files that aren't in the folder. Keep assets relative to the skill directory.
  • Two skills fight: narrow both descriptions so only one matches a given task.

FAQ

Do skills work across repos? User-level skills do; project-level ones travel with the repo.

Can a skill run scripts? Yes, if you ship them and the agent has permission. Read a skill before installing it — that's true for every marketplace.

Where do I find more? Browse the full catalog or start from a task: landing page, pitch deck, launch video.

/skills/agent/cursor.title: Cursor Skills: .cursor/skills vs .agents/skills Explained
/skills/agent/cursor.description: Cursor reads skills from .cursor/skills, .agents/skills or their home-directory equivalents. Which folder wins, how to install, and what to build first.
/skills/agent/cursor.body:
Cursor already knows your codebase. Skills tell it what to produce — a landing page with a specific layout system, a deck with an editorial grid, a set of social cards. The difference between a good Cursor session and a great one is usually whether the taste was written down.

The four folders Cursor reads

ScopePath
Project.cursor/skills/<name>/SKILL.md
Project (shared standard).agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md
User~/.cursor/skills/<name>/SKILL.md
User (shared standard)~/.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md

.agents/skills is the cross-agent location: the same folder works in Cursor, Gemini CLI, Copilot and others. If you use more than one agent, install there once instead of copying files four times.

Install and verify

  1. Copy the skill into .agents/skills/<name>/.
  2. Confirm SKILL.md is directly inside that folder.
  3. Reload the Cursor window.
  4. Ask for the deliverable: "Build a pricing page in this style."

Best first installs for Cursor

SkillWhat it producesInstalls
Cadence Marketing LandingA full marketing page299
Dot Avatar MakerAn interactive avatar builder476
Beacon SaaS LandingA SaaS landing page191
Cobalt Serif Freelancer SiteA portfolio site58
Slate Admin ConsoleAn admin dashboard287
Apple Style OG ImageClean social previews59

Why .agents/skills is the safer default

If you switch agents next quarter — and most teams do — project-scoped .cursor/skills leaves your library behind. .agents/skills is read by Cursor, Gemini CLI and Copilot, so the same investment keeps working. Keep .cursor/skills only for Cursor-specific behaviour.

FAQ

Do project skills get committed? Yes, if the folder isn't gitignored. That's usually what you want for team taste, and usually not what you want for personal experiments.

Can I use a Claude Code skill in Cursor? If it's plain SKILL.md plus assets, yes — copy it into .agents/skills/.

What if a skill overrides my rules? Rules are always-on context; skills are on-demand. Keep style rules in rules, workflows in skills.

/skills/agent/gemini-cli.title: Gemini CLI Skills: .gemini/skills Setup (2026 Guide)
/skills/agent/gemini-cli.description: Gemini CLI reads skills from .gemini/skills or .agents/skills. Exact paths, install steps, and the skills that fit its long-context workflow.
/skills/agent/gemini-cli.body:
Gemini CLI is good at holding a lot of context. Skills keep that context clean: instead of pasting a 900-word brief every time, you install a folder that activates only when the task matches. The agent reads the name and description up front, then loads the body on demand.

Where Gemini CLI looks for skills

ScopePathNotes
Workspace.gemini/skills/<name>/SKILL.mdShared with the repo
Workspace (alias).agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.mdCross-agent standard
User~/.gemini/skills/<name>/SKILL.mdAvailable everywhere
User (alias)~/.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.mdWins over .gemini at the same tier

Within the same tier, the .agents/skills alias takes precedence. Don't keep two copies of the same skill name — you'll spend an afternoon debugging which one loaded.

Install in 30 seconds

  1. Copy the skill folder to .agents/skills/.
  2. Check the path ends with <name>/SKILL.md.
  3. Start a new session and ask for the output you want.
  4. On first use, Gemini CLI asks for consent before loading the skill's files — read the path it shows.

Skills that suit long-context work

SkillWhat it producesInstalls
Chalkboard InfographicA single-page explainer graphic267
Image Narrative DeckA story-led slide deck171
Article Brief DeckA briefing deck from a long article154
Research Talk DeckAn academic talk deck134
Summary Line ChartA clean trend chart53
Article Illustration SetThree consistent illustrations58

A workflow that fits the CLI

Long documents are the point. Feed a PDF or a repo, ask for a briefing deck, then ask for the OG image and the summary chart in the same session. Three skills, one context, no re-explaining.

FAQ

Do skills count against the context window? Only the metadata is always present; the instructions load when activated.

Can I use Claude Code skills here? If they're plain SKILL.md folders, yes — the format is shared.

Where do I start? Article to deck or OG image.

/skills/agent/github-copilot.title: GitHub Copilot Agent Skills: .github/skills Setup
/skills/agent/github-copilot.description: Copilot reads project skills from .github/skills, .claude/skills or .agents/skills, and personal ones from ~/.copilot/skills. Setup and first installs.
/skills/agent/github-copilot.body:
Copilot lives where the code lives, so it's the natural place for skills that encode team conventions: how we build a landing page, how we render a chart, how we produce release assets. Commit the skill once and every contributor's agent inherits the same taste.

Where Copilot looks for skills

ScopePath
Project.github/skills/<name>/SKILL.md
Project (compatible).claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md
Project (cross-agent).agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md
Personal~/.copilot/skills/<name>/SKILL.md
Personal (cross-agent)~/.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md

Copilot supports the same SKILL.md format other agents use, which means a skill library can be shared across a mixed team without rewriting anything.

Install for a team

  1. Create .github/skills/<name>/ in the repo.
  2. Add SKILL.md and any assets next to it.
  3. Commit, open a PR, and mention the skill in the description.
  4. In Copilot Chat, ask for the outcome and reference the file if it doesn't pick it up.

First installs for product teams

SkillWhat it producesInstalls
Beacon SaaS LandingA SaaS marketing page191
Slate Admin ConsoleAn admin UI shell287
Activity Calendar ChartAn activity heatmap component186
Event Bar ChartA responsive bar chart53
Portrait Overlay TestimonialsA testimonial section49
Notion Style OG ImageSocial preview images197

Governance notes

  • Review skills like code: they can ship scripts.
  • Pin versions in the folder name or a version field so a silent update can't change output.
  • Keep personal experiments in ~/.copilot/skills, not in the repo.

FAQ

Does Copilot read Claude skills? Yes, .claude/skills is one of the supported project locations.

Do skills run automatically? They're selected by relevance; scripts only run when the agent executes them, subject to your approvals.

Can I share one library across agents? Put it in .agents/skills — Cursor, Gemini CLI and Copilot all read it.

/skills/agent/windsurf.title: Windsurf Skills: .devin/skills Setup (Legacy .windsurf)
/skills/agent/windsurf.description: Windsurf loads skills from .devin/skills and still reads the legacy .windsurf folder. The precedence rule, the global path, and what to install first.
/skills/agent/windsurf.body:
Windsurf's Cascade is strong at multi-file edits. Skills give it a repeatable definition of done — the layout rules, the export format, the checks to run before handing back a page. If you've ever accepted a beautiful first draft that broke on mobile, a skill is how you stop that from recurring.

Where Windsurf looks for skills

ScopePathNotes
Workspace.devin/skills/<name>/SKILL.mdCurrent location
Workspace (legacy).windsurf/skills/<name>/SKILL.mdStill read as a fallback
Global~/.devin/skills/<name>/SKILL.mdAvailable in all workspaces

Windsurf loads the Devin skills directory when it exists and only falls back to the legacy Windsurf directory when it doesn't. The two are not merged — if you move a skill, move it completely.

Install in 30 seconds

  1. Create .devin/skills/<name>/.
  2. Put SKILL.md and its assets inside.
  3. Reload the workspace.
  4. Ask Cascade for the deliverable, then review the diff.

Common failure

Can I share skills with Cursor users? Yes — put them in .agents/skills, which Cursor and Copilot also read.

Do skills change Cascade's model behaviour? They change what it knows about the task, not which model runs.

/learn/claude-skill-not-loading.title: Claude Skill Not Loading? Check These Five Things
/learn/claude-skill-not-loading.description: A skill that's installed but never triggers is almost always one of five problems. Diagnose folder depth, description match, scope, conflicts and YAML errors.
/learn/claude-skill-not-loading.body:
There are two different failures and they need different fixes:

  • Not discovered — the agent doesn't know the skill exists
  • Not activated — it knows, but decides it isn't relevant

Start by asking the agent to list its skills. If yours isn't there, it's discovery. If it is, it's the description.

1. Folder depth (discovery)

The file must sit directly inside the skill folder:

.claude/skills/og-image/SKILL.md          ✅
.claude/skills/og-image/og-image/SKILL.md ❌
.claude/skills/SKILL.md                   ❌ (no named folder)

Unzipping often creates the extra level. Open the folder and look.

2. Description match (activation)

The model selects skills from the description field alone. If your description is "design helper", a request to "make an OG image" won't match it.

Fix: include the words users actually type.

description: Create 1200x630 OG images and social cards from a title and
  optional screenshot. Use when the user asks for an OG image, link preview,
  social card, or Twitter card.

3. YAML that doesn't parse

A stray tab, an unquoted colon, or a missing --- silently breaks the frontmatter. Paste the block into any YAML validator. If name or description is missing, the skill is invalid.

4. Wrong scope

Project skills live in that repo only. If you installed into .claude/skills inside repo A and you're working in repo B, it isn't there. Global is ~/.claude/skills.

5. Two skills fighting

If two skills have overlapping descriptions, the agent picks one — often not the one you wanted. Narrow both: one owns "OG image", the other owns "YouTube thumbnail".

The 60-second diagnostic

CheckCommand / action
Discovered?Ask the agent to list skills
Depthls .claude/skills/<name>/ shows SKILL.md
YAMLPaste frontmatter into a validator
Scopels ~/.claude/skills vs project folder
ConflictSearch other skills for the same trigger words

Still stuck?

Read the file the agent reads. If the instructions reference references/layouts.md and that file doesn't exist, behaviour becomes unpredictable rather than failing loudly.

/learn/claude-skills-vs-mcp.title: Claude Skills vs MCP: What Actually Differs (2026)
/learn/claude-skills-vs-mcp.description: Skills teach a workflow; MCP connects a system. A concrete comparison with examples, when to use each, when to use both, and how they load at runtime.
/learn/claude-skills-vs-mcp.body:
They're often compared as if they compete. They don't. A Skill is a set of instructions the model reads; MCP is a connection to something outside the model. You can have a great Skill with no MCP, and an MCP server with no Skill. Most useful setups have both.

The one-line difference

**A Skill teaches the agent how to do a job. MCP gives the agent access to a system where the job happens.**

Example: a "publish article" workflow needs an MCP server to reach your CMS, and a Skill that knows your house style, image rules, and slug convention.

Side by side

SkillsMCP
What it isA folder with SKILL.md and optional assetsA protocol + server exposing tools, resources, prompts
Unit of valueProcedural knowledgeCapability / data access
LoadingMetadata up front, body on activationTools listed up front, called on demand
Runs codeCan include scripts; agent executes themServer runs code, agent calls it
Needs a serviceNoYes — a server process or remote endpoint
Typical failureDescription too vague, skill never triggersAuth, permissions, server down
Best forRepeatable output with a point of viewReading/writing data in another system
DistributionCopy a folderInstall and configure a server

What a Skill contains that MCP can't

Taste. A Skill can say "headline at 72 px, never more than five words, accent colour only on the CTA" — and the agent will apply it every time. MCP has no opinion about your design system.

What MCP does that a Skill can't

Live state. A Skill can't read today's orders, post to Slack, or query your warehouse. It can describe how to do those things, but the actual call needs a tool.

When to use each

Use a Skill when:

  • The work is repeatable and has a house style
  • The inputs are files you already have
  • You want the same output next month

Use MCP when:

  • The data lives in another system
  • The result changes minute to minute
  • You need authentication and auditability

Use both when:

  • The workflow spans a system and a format: "pull last week's numbers, then build the chart in our chart style."

A concrete example

Publishing a blog post:

  1. MCP reads the draft from Notion.
  2. Skill checks the house style, writes the meta description, and generates the OG image.
  3. MCP creates the CMS entry.
  4. Skill verifies the slug, canonical and internal links before publishing.

Remove either half and the job breaks.

Common myths

"Skills replace MCP." No. They replace long prompts and Notion docs full of instructions.

"MCP replaces Skills." No. A tool call doesn't carry your standards.

"Skills are just prompts." A prompt is consumed once. A Skill is discovered, versioned, and reused — and can ship scripts and assets.

FAQ

Do Skills need MCP to work? No. Most design and writing skills run entirely on files you provide.

Can a Skill call an MCP tool? It can instruct the agent to use one. The agent still needs the server configured.

Which should I build first? The Skill. It's a text file, it's portable, and it captures the part that's actually yours.

/learn/claude-skills-vs-plugins.title: Claude Skills vs Plugins vs MCP: Which One Do You Need?
/learn/claude-skills-vs-plugins.description: Plugins are a delivery format, Skills are the instructions inside, MCP is the connection to tools. A clear map of the three, with a decision table.
/learn/claude-skills-vs-plugins.h1: Claude Skills vs Plugins vs MCP
/learn/claude-skills-vs-plugins.keyword: claude plugins vs skills vs mcp
/learn/claude-skills-vs-plugins.body:
Three words get mixed together because they arrived at the same time. They operate at different layers:

  • Skill — the instructions for doing a job
  • Plugin — a package that can ship skills, commands, agents, hooks and MCP configuration together
  • MCP — the connection to an external system

Think of a plugin as the box, a skill as the manual inside, and MCP as the power cable.

The layer map

LayerQuestion it answersExample
PluginHow is this distributed and installed?A team plugin that adds three commands, two skills and a review agent
SkillHow should this job be done?"Build an OG image at 1200×630 with our type scale"
MCPWhere does the data come from?A server that reads your CMS

Why the distinction matters

If you only need a repeatable output, a Skill is enough and it's portable across Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI and Copilot. Packaging it as a plugin limits it to one ecosystem.

If you need slash commands, hooks or bundled MCP servers, a plugin is the right container.

Decision table

You want…Build
The same deck style every weekSkill
One-command install for a teamPlugin that contains skills
Read/write to JiraMCP server (+ a Skill for how to use it)
A workflow that spans bothPlugin: Skill + MCP config
Use it in four different agentsSkill in .agents/skills

What's actually inside a plugin

Depending on the ecosystem, a plugin can bundle:

  • skills (including SKILL.md)
  • slash commands
  • subagents
  • hooks
  • MCP server definitions

That's why "plugin vs skill" is a category error: the plugin may contain skills.

Migration advice

Start with a Skill. If you find yourself adding three commands and a hook around it, promote it to a plugin. Don't start with the packaging.

FAQ

Can I use a plugin's skill without the plugin? Usually yes, if it's a plain folder — copy it into your skills directory. Check the license.

Do plugins cost more tokens? They can, if they inject commands and context. Skills only load their metadata until activated.

Which is more future-proof? The SKILL.md folder. It's a file format, not a platform.

/learn/gamma-alternative.title: Gamma Alternative for People Who Want the File
/learn/gamma-alternative.description: Gamma is a hosted deck app. Skills produce an editable file inside your own agent. An honest comparison of workflow, ownership, export and when each one wins.
/learn/gamma-alternative.h1: A Gamma Alternative for People Who Want the File
/learn/gamma-alternative.body:
Gamma is good at what it does: prompt in, presentable deck out, hosted in a browser. The reason people look for an alternative is usually not quality — it's ownership. They want a .pptx they can edit, a repo they can commit, and a workflow that doesn't live in someone else's app.

The real difference

GammaAgent Skills
Where it runsTheir web appYour agent, on your machine
OutputHosted deck, export optionsA file in your project (HTML, PPTX)
CustomisationTemplates and themesEdit the instructions themselves
ReuseRe-prompt each timeVersioned folder
CollaborationIn-appGit / shared drive
Learning curveMinutesMinutes, plus a terminal

When Gamma is the better choice

  • You need a deck in five minutes and don't care about the file
  • You're presenting from a browser
  • You want a polished template library without touching code

When a Skill is the better choice

  • The deck has to match a brand system exactly
  • You need to regenerate it monthly from new data
  • The output must be editable in PowerPoint
  • You want the same instructions across a team

What "editable" actually means

Ask one question: can you click a headline and change the words? If the export is a folder of images, it isn't editable — it's a picture of a deck. Skills that render native text boxes pass this test; ones that screenshot a canvas don't.

A hybrid workflow that works

  1. Draft the storyline in your agent (fast, cheap).
  2. Generate the visual system with a deck skill.
  3. Export to .pptx, check fonts, fix the two slides that broke.
  4. Present from PowerPoint or Google Slides.

You get the speed of AI with a file you own.

FAQ

Is this cheaper? A skill is a one-time file; the model usage is the cost. For heavy use, that's usually less than a per-seat subscription.

Can I import a Gamma deck? Not directly. Rebuild the storyline, then apply a skill's layout system.

Which deck skill first? Field Notes Deck for editorial, Editable Visual Deck if PowerPoint fidelity matters most.

/learn/how-to-install-claude-skills.title: How to Install Claude Skills (Project, Global, Verified)
/learn/how-to-install-claude-skills.description: Exact folders for Claude Code skills, project vs user scope, how to verify a skill loaded, and the four mistakes that make a skill silently do nothing.
/learn/how-to-install-claude-skills.body:
There's no installer to fight. A skill is a folder with a SKILL.md, and installation is putting that folder in the right place. The failures come from where and how deep.

The two locations

ScopePathWho sees it
Project.claude/skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.mdAnyone with the repo
User (global)~/.claude/skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.mdYou, in every project

On Windows, ~ is C:\Users\<you>. If both exist with the same name, the project one wins.

Step by step

  1. Unzip or clone the skill somewhere temporary.
  2. Find SKILL.md. It must be at the root of the skill folder.
  3. Move the folder into .claude/skills/ or ~/.claude/skills/.
  4. Check the depth: .claude/skills/og-image/SKILL.md ✅ — .claude/skills/og-image/og-image/SKILL.md ❌.
  5. Restart Claude Code. Skills are discovered at session start.
  6. Verify: ask "list your skills" or "what skills do you have access to?".

Verify it actually triggers

Listing proves discovery, not activation. Trigger it with a real task:

"Make a 1200×630 OG image for this article, using the og-image skill."

Naming the skill is fine for a test; in daily use, describe the outcome and let the description match.

The four silent failures

1. One folder too deep. The most common. The agent looks for SKILL.md directly inside the skill folder.

2. A vague description. The agent decides whether to load the skill from the description alone. "Helps with design" never matches "make an OG image".

3. Wrong scope. A project skill isn't visible in another repo.

4. No restart. The session read the folder list before you added the file.

Project or global?

Use project for team standards: brand tokens, page templates, review checklists. Use global for personal utilities you want everywhere: OG images, changelogs, commit messages.

Uninstall

Delete the folder. There's no registry and no leftover state. If the skill shipped scripts, also remove anything it wrote outside its folder.

FAQ

Do I need to restart the whole terminal? Restart the agent session; that's enough.

Can I install a skill from a URL? Download the folder and place it manually, or use a CLI that supports one-command install.

Where do other agents look? Cursor, Gemini CLI and Copilot also read .agents/skills; see the agent hubs for exact paths.

/learn/skill-md-format.title: SKILL.md Format: Frontmatter, Limits and a Working Example
/learn/skill-md-format.description: The Agent Skills file format: required name and description fields, length limits, optional license and allowed-tools, plus a complete SKILL.md you can copy.
/learn/skill-md-format.body:
A SKILL.md is Markdown with a YAML frontmatter block. The frontmatter tells the agent when to use the skill; the body tells it how. Get the frontmatter wrong and the best instructions in the world never load.

Minimal valid file

---
name: og-image
description: Create 1200x630 social preview images from a title and optional screenshot. Use when the user asks for an OG image, social card, or link preview.
---

# OG Image

1. Read the title and the page URL.
2. Pick a layout from `references/layouts.md`.
3. Render at 1200x630 with 80px safe margins.
4. Export PNG under 300 KB.

Two fields are required. That's a valid skill.

Field reference

FieldRequiredRules
nameYesMax 64 chars; lowercase letters, numbers, hyphens; no leading/trailing hyphen
descriptionYesMax 1024 chars; non-empty; says what it does and when to use it
licenseNoLicense name or a reference to a bundled file
compatibilityNoMax 500 chars; environment requirements
metadataNoArbitrary key-value pairs (version, author)
allowed-toolsNoRestrict which tools the skill may use

The description is the product

Everything else can be mediocre and the skill still works; a bad description makes it invisible. Write it as: capability + trigger phrases.

Weak:

Helps with images.

Strong:

Create 1200×630 social preview images from a title and optional screenshot. Use when the user asks for an OG image, social card, or link preview.

Body structure that works

  1. One sentence: what this produces
  2. Inputs required
  3. Numbered steps
  4. Output format and constraints
  5. Failure cases ("if no screenshot, use the type-only layout")

Keep it under ~500 lines. If it's longer, move reference material into references/ and load it only when needed.

Optional directories

FolderHoldsLoaded
scripts/Executable helpersOn demand
references/Long docs, checklistsOn demand
assets/Fonts, templates, imagesOn demand

This is progressive disclosure: the agent reads the map first, then opens the drawer it needs.

Validation checklist

  • [ ] Frontmatter parses as YAML
  • [ ] name matches the folder name
  • [ ] description includes at least three phrases a user would actually type
  • [ ] Steps are imperative and ordered
  • [ ] Every referenced file exists
  • [ ] Output format is explicit (size, file type, naming)

FAQ

Can I add custom fields? Yes, under metadata. Unknown top-level fields may be ignored.

Does the filename have to be SKILL.md? Yes, in every implementation I've checked.

Can one skill call another? It can instruct the agent to use another skill, but don't build deep chains — behaviour becomes hard to predict.

/learn/what-are-agent-skills.title: What Are Agent Skills? A Plain-English Explanation
/learn/what-are-agent-skills.description: Agent Skills are folders of instructions an AI agent loads on demand. What's inside, how they differ from prompts and MCP, and why agents adopted one format.
/learn/what-are-agent-skills.body:
An Agent Skill is a folder that teaches an AI agent one job. It contains a SKILL.md with a name, a description, and instructions — plus any templates, references or scripts the job needs. The agent sees the name and description at the start of a session and loads the full instructions only when a task matches.

That's the whole idea. The clever part is what it replaces: a 2,000-word prompt you paste every time, or a Notion page the model never reads.

What's inside

og-image/
  SKILL.md          # name, description, steps
  references/
    layouts.md      # long reference material
  scripts/
    render.ts       # optional helper
  assets/
    font.woff2

Only SKILL.md is required. Everything else is loaded on demand — the agent reads the map first, then opens the drawer it needs.

Why they spread so fast

Because the format is boring. A folder of text files works in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Copilot and Windsurf without a server, an SDK, or a vendor account. The same skill can be committed to a repo and reviewed like code.

Skills vs prompts vs MCP

PromptSkillMCP
LifetimeOne messageReusablePersistent connection
ContainsInstructionsInstructions + assets + scriptsTools and data
LoadedAlwaysOn demandOn demand
PortableCopy-pasteCopy a folderNeeds a server

Use a prompt for a one-off. Use a skill for a job you'll repeat. Use MCP when the job needs live data from another system. More detail: Skills vs MCP.

What makes a good skill

  1. A narrow job. "Make an OG image" beats "help with design".
  2. A description with trigger words. It's the only thing the agent sees before deciding.
  3. Explicit output. Size, format, file name, constraints.
  4. A failure path. What to do when the input is missing.

Where to get them

You can write one in ten minutes, or install one that already encodes a design system. The catalog has 400+ skills across web pages, slides, images and video, each with a preview and an install count.

FAQ

Are skills safe? They're readable text, but they can include scripts. Read before you run — the same rule as any dependency.

Do they work offline? Yes, if the skill and its assets are local and the agent runs locally.

Can I edit a skill? Yes. Fork it and keep your version.

/skills/bs-hyperframes-velocity-sting.body:
Most product clips are a stack of screens with fades between them. This skill's premise is different: every cut is velocity-matched, so seven scenes read as one continuous camera move. It's the difference between a slideshow and a film.

901 installs · v1.0.0 · Video · 2 previews + 1 video

  • A 10–15 second MP4 at your target aspect ratio
  • Seven scenes cut on matching motion vectors
  • Editable source project alongside the render

What you need before you start

  1. Real screens — screenshots or a running page, not mockups.
  2. One action to show — "click generate", not "explore the app".
  3. A target ratio — 16:9 for site, 9:16 for social.
  4. A frame budget — how many seconds each scene gets.

  1. Storyboard. The skill reduces your product to seven shots and asks you to approve them.
  2. Match. It computes matching entry/exit velocity so cuts land on the same vector.
  3. Render. It outputs the film plus the project file so you can retime one beat without rerendering everything.

Good fit: SaaS launches, feature announcements, App Store previews, landing-page heroes.

Before you start

Write five lines: who it's for, the one outcome, the proof you have, the price, and the single action. If you can't fill those in, the page will be beautiful and useless.

Three prompts

1. Structure first — "Before writing code, propose a section outline for a landing page selling [product] to [audience]. For each section, give the headline and the one job it does. Wait for my approval."

2. Then build — "Build the approved outline as a single HTML file. System font stack, max-width 1120 px, 8 px spacing scale, one accent colour. Every button links to #pricing."

3. Then attack it — "Now review your own page at 375 px. List every place text overflows, tap targets under 44 px, or contrast below 4.5:1. Fix them and show the diff."

3. Render. "Build the approved storyboard at 1080×1920, 30 fps, with 120 BPM cuts. Keep the UI legible at 360 px wide."

/skills/task/create-og-image.body:
An OG image is the 1200×630 card that appears when your link is shared. It is not a thumbnail, not a hero image, and not a place to put your entire value proposition. The job is narrower: make someone recognise the link, trust it, and click.

What you get

  • A 1200×630 PNG (or 2400×1260 for retina) under 300 KB
  • Title text inside the safe area — roughly the centre 1080×560
  • Enough contrast to read at 300 px wide in a Slack sidebar
  • A file name that says what it is: groclawa-og-pricing.png

Why most OG images fail

Three predictable reasons: text sits within 40 px of the edge and gets cropped; the title is set at 24 px so it's unreadable in a feed; and the image says the company name but not the promise. Fix those and you're ahead of most SaaS blogs.

Three prompts that work

1. The editorial card — "Create a 1200×630 OG image. Off-white background, one large serif headline in the upper-left, a single product screenshot bleeding off the right edge, and a 2 px rule under the headline. No logo larger than 120 px wide."

2. The data card — "Make an OG image where the number 13,761 is the hero, set at 180 px, with the label 'indexed pages' beneath it in 28 px. Keep 80 px of padding on all sides."

3. The before/after card — "Split the canvas vertically. Left: a plain page screenshot at 40% opacity. Right: the same page with the new design. A 4 px white divider, and a caption in the bottom-left corner."

/skills/task/create-pitch-deck.title: Create a Pitch Deck with AI: Structure Before Slides
/skills/task/create-pitch-deck.description: Most AI decks fail at the storyline, not the design. Build the argument first, then let a Skill render an editable deck you can still change in PowerPoint.
/skills/task/create-pitch-deck.h1: Create a Pitch Deck with AI
/skills/task/create-pitch-deck.body:
Ask an agent for "a 12-slide pitch deck" and you'll get twelve slides of typography with no argument. The deck is a sequence of claims, each earning the next. Write that spine first; the visual system is the easy part.

What you get

  • A deck that exports to .pptx and stays editable
  • One idea per slide, written as an action title
  • A consistent grid, type scale and colour token set
  • Speaker notes for the slides you'll actually talk through

The spine (15 minutes, do this first)

  1. The problem, in the customer's words
  2. Why now
  3. What you do, in one sentence
  4. Proof it works
  5. How you make money
  6. Why you win
  7. The ask

Everything else is support. If a slide doesn't serve one of these, cut it.

Prompts

Structure: "Turn this brief into a 10-slide argument. Each slide gets an action title that states the claim, not the topic. Show me the titles only."

Design: "Render the approved titles using a 12-column grid, one accent colour, and 32 px body text. No stock photos. Use a single chart on slide 5."

Stress test: "You are an investor who has seen 40 decks this month. Which three slides would you push back on, and what evidence is missing?"

Layout: "Build a three-column testimonial grid: 1:1 photo, 24 px quote, name and role in 14 px. Equal heights, no carousel."

Truth check: "Flag any quote that makes a claim we can't substantiate. Suggest a factual replacement."

/skills/task/create-ugc-ad.title: UGC-Style Ads Without an Actor: A Two-Part Workflow
/skills/task/create-ugc-ad.description: There is no single UGC Skill. Build the ad from two parts: social proof that looks real, and motion that keeps it moving. Prompts and honesty rules.
/skills/task/create-ugc-ad.body:
UGC works because it looks like a person, not a brand. If you don't have a person, you have two honest options: build a testimonial-led ad from real customer quotes, or build a screen-led ad that shows the product doing the work. Both convert; fake "customers" don't.

The two-part workflow

Part 1 — proof. A testimonial wall, a quote card, or a before/after. Real names, real photos, real numbers. If you don't have them, use a product demo instead of inventing a person.

Part 2 — motion. A 15-second vertical cut that moves between the proof and the product. Captions on, sound off.

Prompts

Proof: "Build a testimonial section from these three real quotes. Keep the wording exactly as written. One photo per quote, 1:1 crop, no stock imagery."

Cut: "Turn this section into a 15-second 9:16 video: quote 1 for 4s, product screen for 4s, quote 2 for 4s, end card 3s. Captions at 48 px."

Hook test: "Write five first-three-second hooks for this ad. Each must name a specific frustration, not a benefit."

  • If an actor is paid, say so where the platform requires it.
